normalized_name: Trail Estate 'Supersonic' Concord Prince Edward County
gw_description: Concord, Niagara, OntarioFor all our talk about regional grapes from around the world, we hardly talk about one of the grape-iest grape of them all: the Concord! Once the backbone of Ontario's wine industry, this winter-hardy grape was grown for over 150 years until it fell out of favour as wines from California and Europe entered the market. But comebacks are all the rage right now and this scruffy pet-nat reminds us that great things DO grow in Ontario! Sourced from the Lipsitt Vineyard in Niagara, these difficult-to-process grapes undergo several long pressings before being wild fermented to dryness and bottled with unfermented juice to kickstart fermentation in the bottle. Tart, wildberry acid, extra-juicy Welch's fruit, berry crumble, Fruitsations gummies & a touch of earthy funk = the best take on purple Crush we've ever had.

normalized_name: Pearl Morissette 'Roselana' Pinot Noir & Gamay Niagara
gw_description: Pinot Noir & Gamay, Niagara, Ontario Another idiosyncratic classic from the habitual linesteppers at Pearl Morissette, this dark rosé has flirted with being a light red but has instead chosen to bring rigour to the world of whimsical rosés! An unapologetic laugh in the face of being taken lightly, which we love. Grapes spend a brief staycation on their skins before fermenting separately in concrete, texture-giving tanks. They're later blended, aged for another two months in tank to ~come together~ & bottled unfined and unfiltered. Lipstick kiss on the vanity, cherry Lipsmacker, cherry pot pie, ushy gushy strawberry with an offbeat kick in its step until you realize that it's totally dry and thus, totally lean & sexy despite the aforementioned exuberance. An all-weather rosé with the freshness of a white & the structure of a red, pair with pork tenderloin, the white meat of red meats, another genre-bender!

gw_description: Gamay, Niagara, Canada Celebrate THIS YEAR'S HARVEST with our freshest Ontario House drop, 2025 gamay. Enjoy anytime, anywhere, anyhow, preferably with a chill from dawn til dusk remembering the fall, setting intentions for the spring and thanking nature for her bounty.

gw_description: L'Acadie Blanc & Cabernet Franc, Niagara, Ontario, Canada Earthy, verdant and zero-zero, 'Caravaggio' is the latest wine released by visionary Ontario winemaker Drea Scotland! Driven, unendingly knowledgable and KEY industry advocate, Drea Scotland's project Drinks Farm, is all about grounding curiosity, newfound sensory experiences & utilizing the best local ingredients. FUN FACT! Drea's 2024 vintage, as well as the next few vintages, will be made entirely from purchased grapes (aka négoce), until her freshly-planted, baby hybrid vineyard in Prince Edward County starts producing! A 50/50 blend of direct-pressed hybrid white grape mineral, tree-fruity l'acadie blanc from Appleton Farm in Thornbury, plus whole-cluster, carbonically macerated (for one whole month!) herbaceous, mineral cab franc from Heather Laundry in Niagara. FUN FACT #2! The cab franc was partially dried on the vine for super DEEP concentration and only 71 cases were made! Hits of reduction add a weightless suspension to the full mouthful of deep, brambly fruit awaiting you, soil, fallen tree trunk, old leaves, young leaves, green pears, dandelion, burlap, bumpy roads & small wisdoms. Chill and pour the night before your next road trip, cheers to never losing your sense of adventure. #goodthingsgrowinontario

normalized_name: Ontario House 'Raver Dave's Cab Franc' Cabernet Franc Niagara
producer: Ontario House 'Raver Dave's Cab Franc' Cabernet Franc
gw_description: Cabernet Franc, Niagara, Ontario, Canada Meet RAVER DAVE'S! A lip-smacking, spicy and satisfying Niagara cab franc that is part power, part deep fruit. Made in collaboration with our darling pals over at Paradise Grapevine and a part of our Ontario House project bringing well priced, interesting and delicious local wines to your table. This year's 'Raver Dave's' indulges in the dense concentration of the 2024 harvest, a landmark year for cabs in Ontario! Made from two parcels at Willms Vineyard in Four Mile Creek, one younger plot (60%) bringing LIVELY juiced-up flare, the other 37 years-old, harvested late (after the first frost) and showing more classically rich, brooding and with a concentration of sugar (40%), both of which were aged in barrel for ten months prior to blending. Ready for your next rave (obvi), family brunch or horror film marathon.

gw_description: Verdeho o Original, Azores, Portugal A salty, volcanic and entirely unique Portuguese white to take you back in time! Worldly winemaker Antonio Maçanita works to capture the essence of regional terroir and traditions through the grapes that move him from the island of Pico, which is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Home to unique, volcanic basalt soils, the Azores is a Portuguese archipelago where wine has been made since the 15th century when it was introduced by Franciscan friars. FUN FACT! This bottle is made from verdelho o original, or verdelho do pico, a species endemic to Azores and Madeira! Grown on volcanic basalt soils, the 15 to 35-year-old, rarely seen grape vines were harvested and whole bunch pressed for eight months of texture-promising lees contact. Literally blew us away with how unique and DELICIOUS. Guava pop, seaside herbs and grasses, pink grapefruit, whole passionfruit, lemon rind & tossing beach stones. Pour alongside the freshest shellfish you can get your mitts on.

raw_wine_line: Clai 'Baracija' Malvasia, Istria, Croatia
normalized_name: Clai 'Baracija' Malvasia Istria
gw_description: Malvasia, Istria, Croatia A fleshy, dense and aromatic Croatian malvasia for springtime spectacles. From the northern part of the Istrian peninsula, close to the Slovenian and Italian border, Clai encompasses 10 hectares of vineyards and 5 hectares of olive trees, 200 metres above sea level. The malvasia grapes for 'Baracija' are hand picked from their limestone flysch soils, composed of thin layers of hard limestone and soft shale/mudston. They're then de-stemmed and moved with their skins to large wooden barrels for 7-20 days of maceration, before 12 months in large oak foudres. Wet hay meets pressed flowers, flint, fall honey, barley stalks, white pear, sea salt, white melon balls & yellow dragon fruit. Pour alongside tending to your forsythia bush.

Stick this ripe beauty into the snow, slush or semi-deep puddle to chill down and consume while shovelling snow or folding laundry.

normalized_name: Séléné 'Primeur' Gamay Beaujolais
gw_description: Gamay, Beaujolais, France A berried, earthy & JUICY big bojo baby! After interning at Savoie's famed Belluard and Beaujolais's great Lapalu, ex-punk rocker Sylvère Trichard began Séléné in his hometown of Blacé, with farmer and friend Elodie Bouvard in 2012. Since then the property has flourished with plantings of fruits, and vegetables, as well as the introduction of animals and biodynamic practices. From Sylvère's home block on sandy pink granite, the young vines are picked by hand and carbonically macerated in concrete tank for five days to amp up aromatics and JUICINESS, before being pressed off to finish fermentation. FUN FACT! Essentially right after the wine is dry and through malolactic conversion, it is bottled and released young & HUNGRY in the great Beaujolais Nouveau tradition! Melange of red and black liquorice, mashed strawberries, baked blueberry + underripe blueberries + yoghurt, wood bark structure, cranberry & a stemmy scruffiness. Pour alongside cowboy omelettes and spring flowers.

normalized_name: Pardas 'Rupestris' Xarel-lo & Malvasía de Sitges Penedes
gw_description: Xarel-lo & Malvasia de Sitges, Penedés, Spain An earthen, bright & nuanced Spanish white blend for the wild pig in all of us. The terribly exciting Catalonian wine project, Celler Pardas, is named after the wild boars that roam the 30 hectares of Mediterranean forests surrounding their painstakingly restored vineyards. Working out of an ancient cellar, Ramon Parera and Jordi Anan cultivate historical grape varieties like sumoll and xarel-lo with the gentlest touch. Coming from limestone slopes, 'Rupestris' is a direct-pressed white blend composed of citric, mineral xarel-lo and rare, aromatic and fruit-forward malvasia de sitges, that spent some time rooting around in chestnut barrels. FUN FACT! Malvasia de sitges is a historical variety, believed to be of Greek origin and now protected in the Sitges area! Stonewall hiding a flower garden, fennel fronds and rosemary greenery, orchard picnic, lemongrass, chamomile, whole lemon, a runny honey consistency & salted pineapple richness. Pour alongside rolling your own sushi for the first time.

raw_wine_line: Gut Oggau 'Winifred' Blaufränkisch & Rotburger, Burgenland, Austria
normalized_name: Gut Oggau 'Winifred' Blaufränkisch & Rotburger Burgenland
gw_description: Blaufränkisch & Rotburger, Burgenland, Austria Gut Oggau winemakers Stephanie & Eduard Tscheppe are deeply adored by natural wine lovers the whole world over and deserve every last iota of praise & reverence they receive. The fabric of the wines hinges upon the existence of a fictional family, with every vineyard plot being characterized by one of its members. Sometimes the cleverness of this device can call attention away from how consistently elegant, bewitching & functional these wines truly are, and either way, the Gut Oggau fam is way more than a cutesy gimmick— it's a progressive and anti-patriarchal language for thinking about wine emotionally & intuitively, which we are obviously way here for. Winifred is definitely the secret and most effortlessly coolest member of the Gut Oggau fam like a Cat Power/Patti Smith vibes tomboy poet who can repair a car engine with the same degree of natural ease as she can quote entire passages from Finnegan's Wake. Darker, riper, and more candied than the previous vintage, ALIVE with trapped CO2, herbaceous glimpses, rosy reduction, MEGA STRAWBERRY, ranier cherry bite, cool blue minerality, lemon gatorade & hand chiseled ice sculptures. Fermentation takes place in used oak barrels; the wine goes through elevage in said barrels for about 8 months, with no batonnage. Winifred is then bottled unfined, unfiltered, and with zero addition of sulphur.

raw_wine_line: Guimaro 'Mencia Joven' Mencia, Ribeira Sacra, Spain
normalized_name: Guimaro 'Mencia Joven' Mencia Ribeira Sacra
gw_description: Mencía, Ribeira Sacra, Spain From rugged Spanish terrain, may we present an earthy, aromatic and spiced mencía that is endlessly charming & simply tastes FANCY. Founded by Manolo and Carmen Rodriguez in 1991, the estate is run today by their son Pedro Rodriguez, who took over in the early 2000s. Pedro's first order of business was to convert the eight hectares of picturesque and treacherous (think STEEP and terraced) vineyards to organic production, while also lowering yields and focusing on quality. This 40-year-old mencía comes from different plots of slate, granite and sand. Grapes are macerated 20% whole cluster and 80% destemmed for six days before spending six months on lees gaining complexity. French lavender, butterly pea blossom, barberry pie, blueberry jellies, liquorice root, mud, puff of smoke & a spicy n' dicey ending. Enjoy alongside hefty entrees and empty ballroom dances.

raw_wine_line: Thymiopoulos 'Xinomavro Nature' Xinomavro, Naoussa, Greece
normalized_name: Thymiopoulos 'Xinomavro Nature' Xinomavro Naoussa
gw_description: Xinomavro, Naoussa, Greece A vegetal, stoney and spiced piece of Grecian history, plus a GW exlusive for Ontario! This was a favourite of our colleagues when they visited the winery last year, and we're so chuffed to have it here after many months of waiting. Apostolis Thymiopoulos's love affair with xinomavro, the star regional grape of Naoussa, is one for the ages. His family has been grape-growing for generations in the small village of Trilofos, where today he makes 10 different expressions of the same grape, xinomavro in an effort to showcase its dynamic and diverse star power. FUN FACT! The warm climate is tempered by the Mediterranean winds and air flowing down from the nearby Vermio mountain creating surprising freshness in this rich region. This zero-sulphur added GW Ontario exclusive was harvested from 50 year-old vines, 70% of the grapes were left whole cluster for a 30-day maceration and fermentation, then spent 12 months aging in newer wood barrels for structure. Mouthful of strawberries, tomato juice, black olive, home-fermented tonic water, spunky spices, bay leaf, tobacco & stoney rubble. Pour alongside game meat burgers and beef tallow fries for a touch of wilderness.

gw_description: Piemonte, Italy A salty, savoury and magnificently seasonal Italian dry vermouth. GWI's first aperitif and digestif producer is back with a BRAND NEW cuvée, buongiorno Chinati Vergano! Tomasso and Pietro Vergano are second-generation makers, creating small batches of balanced and unique elixirs out of a teeny facility in Torino. These earthly delights are made from a base of natural wine sourced from many of our grape-growing heroes, and infused with carefully chosen, regionally significant and internationally treasured botanicals, herbs, citrus & spices. The cheeky 'Sec' is brand-new to the lineup, and differs from its siblings in that it is their only vermouth to be made with a non-Italian wine base (the base is estate romorantin from their close friend Thierry Puzelat of Clos du Tue Boeuf in the Loire Valley!) and is the first of their vermouths whose extract (called "concia" in Italian) is prepared from mainly fresh, seasonal, organic ingredients, as opposed to their usual dried botanicals that permit year-round production. FUN FACT! By working with fresh, seasonal ingredients, 'Sec' takes about a year to build! First, citrons are harvested for their fresh peels in January, then wild elderflower and acacia flowers in spring, raspberries in July, fig leaves at summer's end (used both fresh and dried) & the almond-y kernels from inside fresh peach pits (they pick the peaches, dry the pits and crush them to obtain the kernels), all macerated separately, layered throughout the year and culminating in 75% of the "concia", while the other 25% is built from dried ingredients like wormwood and peppercorns. Salty and verdant, white pepper, seaweed, brushed minerality, dragon fruit, oregano, white grape, lemon jello & playing with an early 2000s potion-making game. Enjoy with one cube, a twist of lemon or sprig of thyme and a riveting conversation about the value of third spaces.

raw_wine_line: Laurent Saillard 'Blank' Sauvignon Blanc, Loire, France
normalized_name: Laurent Saillard 'Blank' Sauvignon Blanc Loire
gw_description: Sauvignon Blanc, Loire, France A balanced, rare and gossamer treat for the Loire-leaning or soon to be Loire-lover. Laurent's wines are emotive, spirited and, as of late, created out of determination in the face of climate instability and destruction by frost, hail or rain. 2023 was also a challenging, small vintage, but what remained is singing and we're chuffed to offer Laurent's top white wine 'Blank' for the very first time. Two versions of this wine exist, one a solera started in 2018, one a vintage rendition, and this is the vintage coming in BLANC HOT from 2023. Sun-shiney 70-year-old sauv blanc vines from Laurent's parcel of the famed Clos Roche Blanche vineyard were hand harvested, direct pressed, then stashed away in 400 L barrels for one year. Gunshot on a spring morning in a silent film kinda reduction, vanilla cotton candy, lemon and strawberry juice freezie, cool blue slate & a chewable plushness that breaks away from the herd to leave us in a lengthy mineral lean-ness. Enjoy while contemplating your current blank canvas, be it a bathroom, a forgotten garden or a patch of un-inked skin.

raw_wine_line: Es d'Aqui 'Illumi-Nat', Mauzac, Languedoc-Roussillon, France
normalized_name: Es d'Aqui 'Illumi-Nat' Mauzac
gw_description: Mauzac, Languedoc-Rousillon, France A gentle, free-thinking and zero-zero pet-nat with historic roots! Jean-Louis Pinto has operated his negociant (he purchases fruit rather than farming it) project since 2010. Based near Limoux, he sources organic and biodynamically tended grapes from unique plots, while working out of a small cellar beneath his family home. There is no set style applied year-to-year, but you are guaranteed to be surprised, delighted & (like we are) infatuated vintage after vintage. FUN FACT! Before there was Champagne there was "Blanquette Méthode Ancestrale" (also called "Blanquette de Limoux"), a bubbly wine made in this region out of mauzac grapes that was first recorded being produced by monks in 1531! The grapes here were sourced from over 80-year-old mauzac vines grown high up on the only limestone portion of this mountainside vineyard, overlooking a valley in Campagne-sur-Aude, Limoux. The grapes were macerated for six days and bottled before fermentation was complete to trap enlivening C02, then aged for 14 months on lees before disgorging (removal of lees/sediment). Fine, filigree nose of minerals and pear blossoms, apple crisp topped with tart pear-sauce, chalky sweethearts, leesy weight, grey rocks & tearing into a packet of Euro white gummies. Pour alongside breakfast buffets with anything from caviar topped eggs to syrup-soaked flapjacks.

gw_description: Domina & Müller-Thurgau, Franken, Germany A refreshing, savoury German rotling for the making of new memories. Chefs turned winemakers Emily Campeau and Christoph Müller are all about polyculture cultivation, gustatorily amicable ferments & creative, almost recipe-like assemblage. 'Newstalgia' is a rotling, a fresh style of wine from the old days that blends red and white grapes. This is their contribution to its second wind, nostalgia… more like NEWSTALGIA! FUN FACT! This bottle is sealed with organic beeswax from Christoph's village in Württemberg! A 50/50 blend of berried, earthy domina and floral, herbaceous müller-thurgau purchased from a friend going through organic certification. The grapes were destemmed and blended together for a three day maceration. They started to ferment lightly before pressing, before being aged for 11 months in used barrels and six months in bottle before coming to us. Cranberries in a cave, mountainside herbs, cherry viscosity, strawberry jam familiarity, a homemade paper texture & cooling minerality. Enjoy with a plate of spiced and roasted beetroots.

raw_wine_line: Bruno Duchene 'La Lune Rouge' Grenache, Carignan & Friends, Banyuls-sur-Mer, France
normalized_name: Bruno Duchene 'La Lune Rouge' Grenache Carignan & Friends
gw_description: Grenache Noir, Grenache Gris, Grenache Blanc & Carignan, Languedoc-Roussillon, France A rare, animated and zero-zero Banyuls red-white blend that just may have fallen to Earth from the far reaches of outer space. Fresh in from Grape Witch Imports, the wines of Bruno Duchêne are now available in Ontario for the very first time! Previously a SUCCESSFUL mushroom grower, Bruno retired in his early 40s and began making wine in 2002 when he became bored of retired life. Today he tends to his 4.5, schist-y hectares of over 50-year-old, terraced vines with as little intervention as possible. FUN FACT! He lives on his boat Odin most of the year! A blend of 50-year-old, berried, herbaceous grenache noir, rich, mineral grenache gris, aromatic, tart grenache blanc (90%), and earthy, spiced carignan (10%) grown on a dozen different schist-laden plots in Banyuls-sur-Mer. The grapes were all left whole cluster for a 10-15 day maceration, then aged for six months between wooden barrels and stainless steel tanks for a mix of freshness and fullness. Symphonic, minty tingles, rose petals, thyme, purslane, purple and yellow plums meets raspberry, dusty jewels pulled from a dusty chest, blood orange bitters & black sand tannins and minerality. Pour alongside stargazing and planting your moon garden.

producer: Villa Picta 'Sognare Sognare' Lambrusco di Sorbara
gw_description: Lambrusco di Sorbara, Lombardy, Italy A romantically rich, balanced and crowd pleasing Valentine's Day ready lambrusco if we've ever tasted one! Young, passionate winegrower and maker Paolo Pasini, and author/NYC *star* sommelier Amanda Smeltz have teamed up and are representing lambrusco in new, sincere and groundbreaking ways. 'Sognare! Sognare!' is a champagne method Lambrusco made with lambrusco di sorbara, the closest to the wild or 'sylvestris' origins of the lambrusco vine which is known for its bright, refreshingly high acidity. FUN FACT! Translating to "to dream, to dream", the name is taken from a song by Italian '70s prog rock band PFM, and represents the fulfillment of Paolo's teenage dream of making a Champagne-method rosato from Lambrusco di Sorbara, to which we respond, what a teenager! Aged on lees in bottle for at least 20 months before hand-disgorging, the wine is further aged three-to-six months before release to ensure it is settled and showing its best. Lush n' leesy, caramelized cherries, perfectly balanced tartness, translucent tannins, rose petals tea, strawberry patch & a fine, creamy mousse. Pour alongside a romantic date with your long-term partner, blind date, friend-group potluck or your precious, precious self. Xoxoxoxo, GW.

gw_description: Nebbiolo, Lombardy, Italy A vibrant, mineral and ethereal alpine nebbiolo for the thrill-seeking downhill skier in all of us. Founded in 2019 while working at the world famous ArPePe, Marco Ferrari is a small and gleaming jewel of an estate in the glacier-formed, river-carved Valtellina. High up in the mountains, Valtellina is known for their remarkably steep, time-worn stone-terrace vineyards and wines of cool elegance, and Marco works them with one foot in tradition and another digging-in for dear life to the exhilarating slopes. FUN FACT! The nebbiolo is sourced from a few different plots in Sassella and Inferno that rest on metamorphic soils of sand, gneiss and mica schist; these offer enhanced heat retention and provide good drainage, often leading to riper, more intense, and structurally complex wines! 2024 was a cool vintage, and the grapes were left 30% whole cluster for three days of semi-carbonic maceration perking up aromatics, followed by 13 days on the skins for tactility, and then aged in a mixture of concrete (70%) and large wooden cask (30%) for eight months to bridge all the gaps. Every liquorice flavour wound together, cherry, raspberry…red perfection, a tiny jaw-snapping natty snarl, light cacao dusting, soft herbs, rushing minerality & scrappy tannins that claw at you playfully. Pour alongside porcini risotto and The Mushroom at the End of the World by Anna Tsing.
